text:
nora: Heads up 1: multiple customers filing tickets saying SDKs show 429 but Console shows a red outage badge for same minute ranges. They9re unsure if they should back off or expect a sustained outage.

diego: Oof. Are these the cases where router first serves a cheaper model then later rejects because tenant budget is exceeded? We9ve had chains like fallback -> quota_reject in a single request window.

hana: Yep. Currently we emit separate telemetry events (fallback.model, quota.reject). The UI picks the last event to set the badge; SDKs use the first HTTP status returned. That mismatch causes the UX gap.

product-ian: We need a single, customer-facing signal that answers: "should I retry now?" vs "do I need to contact support/sales?" The Console and SDKs must tell the same story.

sdk-rita: SDKs prefer code-first flow control. We should not rely on freeform message strings. A small header + clear HTTP code mapping is ideal. Also add a structured JSON header for advanced clients.

nora: Suggestion: emit x-rd-client-status (enum: "retryable","degraded","blocked") plus x-rd-meta (semi-colon list) with source and retry_after when applicable. HTTP code must reflect the most actionable state: if blocked -> 403/429, if degraded -> 206 or 503 depending on output change, if fully OK -> 200.

diego: Concrete mappings proposal:
- quota.block -> 429 + x-rd-client-status=retryable; retry_after=XX;source=quota
- fallback_to_lower_model -> 206 + x-rd-client-status=degraded; source=router;model=small
- reject_after_fallback -> 503 + x-rd-client-status=blocked; source=router
- account_suspended -> 403 + x-rd-client-status=blocked; source=account

hana: I9d avoid 200 with warnings. If the output is materially lower quality we should indicate non-2xx so customers can programmatically surface banners. 206 fits nicely for partial/altered responses.

product-ian: For Console: derive badge from the highest-severity status across the request window: blocked > degraded > retryable > ok. Also surface a single human-friendly message and a primary action: "Retry" for retryable, "Switch plan/contact sales" for blocked, "Expect lower fidelity" for degraded.

sdk-rita: On SDK side, we9ll expose a structured object parsed from headers: rdStatus: {state, source, retryAfter}, plus boolean shouldRetry. shouldRetry true only for retryable. We'll add helper backoff util.

diego: Telemetry rename: emit rd.client_severity with labels severity=blocked|degraded|retryable and actor=router|quota|model. That helps alert rules and dashboards to align with UX.

hana: Need tests: create synthetic trace where request triggers fallback then a reject afterwards; assert SDK sees first non-2xx that requires action and console shows blocked badge (highest severity).

product-ian: UX copy drafts:
- retryable: "Temporary capacity limit. Retry after {n}s or use exponential backoff."
- degraded: "We served a lower-capacity model to meet latency targets. Output quality may be reduced."
- blocked: "Request blocked due to quota/account restrictions or service outage. See runbook or contact support."

sdk-rita: Plan: implement header + telemetry (feature-flagged) -> update SDK parsing (flagged) -> run end-to-end test in staging -> flip on console derivation. We9ll also ship migration notes and examples.

nora: Ops: infra-bot schedule: headers-flag -> staging 03:00 UTC tomorrow, run smoke & synthetic tests for 3 hours, then prod 24h later if green.

infra-bot: scheduled: headers-flag rollout staging at 2026-03-22T03:00:00Z. Auto-promote window 24h after successful smoke.

diego: One more ask: include a short troubleshooting table in the Console runbook mapping header+http -> recommended user action. That will reduce support churn.

hana: Will add RFC doc with header schema, examples, telemetry labels, and Prometheus/ES alert mappings.

product-ian: Great. Once RFC lands, I9ll update Console copy and tie runbook links to the badge actions.

sdk-rita: I9ll open the SDK PR and tag this thread when ready.

nora: Thanks everyone. This should cut down on confused tickets. Keeping watch on the staging run and will report back. :thumbsup:
